headline: Vice President Compliance Product Officer
about: Seasoned financial services attorney with a focus on mortgage servicing and title insurance law.  Extensive knowledge of RESPA, TILA, FDCPA, ECOA, FHA, ADA, FCRA, SCRA and UDAAP as well as investor (GSE, USDA, FHA and VA) and state law servicing requirements including, but not limited to, debt collection, loss mitigation and escrow requirements.  In addition to advising the business on regulatory compliance issues, experience includes resolving complaints and managing outside counsel in litigation matters.

experience.description: Conducted complete overhaul of the Company's loss mitigation procedure from ground up which entailed meeting with multiple departments to define roles and processes, creation of new policies and procedures and development of new borrower communications to ensure compliance with federal, state and investor requirements.  Other roles included responding to federal and state regulatory investigations and examinations, supporting the QWR team with regard to complaint resolution,  advising business with regard to gaps in processes and need for remediation,  implementing new policies and procedures and changes to existing policies and procedures in response to changes in regulatory and investor requirements, review and approval of communications and participation in multiple servicing-related projects.

Served as part of compliance team.  Responsible for educating various business units on agency requirements; development of policies and procedures covering a wide variety of subject matter, including but not limited to, loss mitigation, collections, mortgage insurance cancellation, escrow requirements, SCRA requirements and foreclosure;  advising business units on regulatory changes and overseeing the implementation of compliant processes; responding to regulatory investigations and examinations; and identifying gaps in existing processes, assessing risk and developing remediation plans.

Subject matter expert on loss mitigation in the Servicing Legal department providing support to the loss mitigation, modification and collateral business units.  Part of high priority task team responsible for implementing measures related to the  COVID-19 pandemic.  Daily responsibilities included advising the business teams on federal, state and investor requirements and the means to implement compliant operations;  analyzing escalated issues and providing direction for resolution; responding to federal and state regulatory investigations and inquiries from investors and private label servicing clients; identifying gaps in processes and determining the severity of risks, root cause and the need for remediation and action plans to resolve identified issues; drafting and providing guidance on loss mitigation letter templates, call scripts and website content; conducting regular calls with the loss mitigation teams to discuss topics and resolution of issues; reviewing and revising policy and procedure updates and reviewing vendor contracts and templates.

Worked on-site for primary client, Fannie Mae.  Responsibilities included serving as liaison between REO title group and Fannie Mae legal department; providing advice to various Fannie Mae departments regarding, among other things, title, closing and sales issues involved in the marketing and sale of REO nationwide; managing a large nationwide portfolio of litigation matters involving a wide spectrum of issues including code violations, insurance claims and issues with HOA's, Co-ops and title related matters; working closely with outside counsel, title underwriters and servicers to resolve legal problems related to the marketing and sale of REO properties, foreclosures and distressed loans.  Extensive knowledge of Fannie Mae's procedures, including its selling and servicing guides and REO sales contracts and guidelines.
Retained as consulting expert in defalcation matter on behalf of Lawyers Title Insurance Corporation and its litigation counsel, Figari and Davenport.

Reviewed and administered claims on behalf of Commonwealth Land Title Insurance Company and Lawyers Title Insurance Corporation.  Retained and managed counsel in representation of insured owners and lenders in litigation in multiple states including Texas, Oklahoma, Missouri and Kansas.  Knowledge of multiple areas of law, including but not limited to, real estate, probate, family law, finance and bankruptcy. Represented insurance underwriters and subsidiaries in mediations and escrow disputes.

Reviewed and administered claims on behalf of Fidelity National Title Insurance Company, Chicago Title Insurance Company, Security Union Title Insurance Company, Ticor Title Insurance Company and ALamo Title Insurance Company.  Managed average monthly portfolio of approximately 250 files in multiple states including Texas, Florida, Colorado, New Mexico, North Carolina and South Carolina.  Represented the Fidelity Companies in mediations and instructed outside counsel concerning matters in litigation.   Prepared papers and spoke at seminars concerning title insurance claim issues.

about:
My mission in life is to help individuals improve all areas of their life whether is physical, emotional, spiritual or financial through the power of personal growth and leadership training.   

2020 uncovered a new found passion, to advocate specifically in the area of Financial Literacy

An early start in wealth management and the law firm industry, ignited my passion to inspire professionals and busy individuals improve their work life balance.  Mental Health and Financial Literacy, although connected, these  areas are easily neglected by many and the most requested topics in my speaking engagements along with personal growth. 

Having the opportunity to work at a law firm at age 16, allowed me to realize the importance of a support system and an influential inner circle.  Since then, I’ve surrounded myself by strong leaders that encourage me to break barriers and achieve success.  I’ve measured their influence in my life by accomplishments in my personal and professional careers from wealth management to sales, marketing, business development, strategic planning, project management, public relations, international trade, financial services, business consulting, relationship building, speaking, training, coaching and fitness services.  

My personal commitment now is to share what I’ve learned and add value to others.

I’m a passionate philanthropist and have been fortunate to have served in leadership roles in several non-for profits.  My involvement with organizations such as the National Youth Advocate Program, Family Bridges, A Safe Haven Foundation, A Gift of Value, The World Trade Center, The Maxwell Leadership Enterprise, Equip and the ELISA Foundation, have allowed me to give back and empower individuals through my speaking, training and coaching services nationally and internationally. 

Some of my favorites things to do is travel, read, exercise and spend quality time with my family.  

Let’s connect if it feels right.

publications.title: Financial integration within Europe and the international transmission of business cycles among industrialized countries
publications.description: We exploit a dataset on financial integration within Europe to answer a novel question in the international Real Business Cycle (RBC) literature. Does financial integration within Europe matter for the international transmission of business cycles between the United States and Europe? We find that it does, and that as European countries become more financially integrated among themselves, European business cycles start to ‘decouple’ from those in the United States. We show that this is true for three macro indicators of economic activity: Gross Domestic Product (GDP), consumption and investment, and for five alternative measures of the degree of financial integration. We also show that the effect of trade linkages becomes insignificant once financial factors are accounted for. Our work has interesting policy implications since it unveils the importance of further integration in the EU to slow down the transmission of aggregate shocks among industrialized nations.

Recognized leader that can manage top performing teams and multi-million dollar portfolios. publications.title: The Impact of Spatial Aggregation Error on the Spatial Scan Analysis: A Case Study of Colorectal Cancer
publications.description: The paper aims to estimate the level and impact of spatial aggregation error for spatial scan statistics where disaggregated data below the zip code level are not available. Data on colorectal cancer cases in Cook county, Illinois, USA with a 5-year interval were used. An innovative procedure using SAS and Java was designed to make SaTScan auto-run. Characteristics of clusters at each reference level were compared to those at zip code level to observe differences related to spatial aggregation. The comparison reveals that spatial scan statistic at the zip code level can generate reliable clusters in areas with a large number of cases, but fail to detect clusters in areas where there are a sparse number of cases, since the spatial aggregation error is minimised in areas with sizeable numbers of cases. Without localised cancer data, zip code level data can be used effectively to identify dominant clusters. However, smaller clusters located in low-density areas may be missed.

publications.title: Spatial Error in Geocoding Physician Location Data from the AMA Physician Masterfile: Implications for Spatial Accessibility Analysis
publications.description: This paper examines spatial errors that arise due to incorrect address information with respect to physician location data in the United States. Studies of spatial accessibility to physicians in the U.S. typically rely on data from the American Medical Association’s Physician Masterfile. These data are problematic because a substantial proportion of physicians only report a mailing address, which is often the physician’s home (residential) location, rather than the address for the location where health care is provided. The incorrect geocoding of physicians’ practice locations based on inappropriate address information results in a form of geocoding error that has not been widely analyzed. Using data for the Chicago metropolitan region, we analyze the extent and implications of geocoding error for measurement of spatial accessibility to primary care physicians. We geocode the locations of primary care physicians based on mailing addresses and office addresses. The spatial mismatch between the two is computed at the county, zip code and point location scales. Although mailing and office address locations are quite close for many physicians, they are far apart (>20 km) for a substantial minority. Kernel density estimation is used to characterize the spatial distribution of physicians based on office and mailing addresses and to identify areas of high spatial mismatch between the two. Errors are socially and geographically uneven, resulting in overestimation of physician supply in some high-income suburban communities, and underestimation in certain central city locations where health facilities are concentrated. The resulting errors affect local measures of spatial accessibility to primary care, biasing statistical analyses of the associations between spatial access to care and health outcomes

publications.title: Rural-Urban Inequalities in Late-stage Breast Cancer: Spatial and Social Dimensions of Risk
publications.description: Rural – urban inequalities in health and access to health care have long been of concern in health-policy formulation. Understanding these inequalities is critically important in efforts to plan a more effective geographical distribution of public health resources and programs. Socially and ethnically diverse populations are likely to exhibit different rural – urban gradients in health and well-being because of their varying experiences of place environments, yet little is known about the interplay between social and spatial inequalities. Using data from the Illinois State Cancer Registry, we investigate rural – urban inequalities in late-stage breast cancer diagnosis both for the overall population and for African-Americans, and the impacts of socioeconomic deprivation and spatial access to health care. Changes over time are analyzed from 1988–92 to 1998–2002, periods of heightened breast cancer awareness and increased access to screening. In both time periods, the risk of late-stage diagnosis is highest among patients living in the most urbanized areas, an indication of urban disadvantage. Multilevel modeling results indicate that rural – urban inequalities in risk are associated with differences in the demographic characteristics of area populations and differences in the social and spatial characteristics of the places in which they live. For African-American breast cancer patients, the rural – urban gradient is reversed, with higher risks among patients living outside the city of Chicago, suggesting a distinct set of health-related risks and place experiences that inhibit early breast cancer detection. Findings emphasize the need for combining spatial and social targeting in locating cancer prevention and treatment programs.

publications.title: Socio-Spatial Inequalities in Late-Stage Cancer Diagnosis in Illinois: Spatial Temporal Trends and Methodological Challenges: Ph.D. Dissertation
publications.description:
This dissertation examines the effects of social and spatial inequalities on late-stage diagnosis of
colorectal and breast cancer, and it addresses several methodological challenges surrounding the use of ZIP codes as a study unit in analyzing late-stage cancer at diagnosis. Given that my dissertation follows the three-paper‘ format, the abstract section is divided into three parts to describe each paper respectively.

publications.title: Analyzing Spatial Aggregation Error in Statistical Models of Late-Stage Cancer Risk: A Monte Carlo Simulation Approach
publications.publishedAt: International Journal of Health Geographics · Jan 1, 2010
publications.description:
Purpose
This paper examines the effect of spatial aggregation error on statistical estimates of the association between spatial access to health care and late-stage cancer.

Methods
Monte Carlo simulation was used to disaggregate cancer cases for two Illinois counties from zip code to census block in proportion to the age-race composition of the block population. After the disaggregation, a hierarchical logistic model was estimated examining the relationship between late-stage breast cancer and risk factors including travel distance to mammography, at both the zip code and census block levels. Model coefficients were compared between the two levels to assess the impact of spatial aggregation error.

Results
We found that spatial aggregation error influences the coefficients of regression-type models at the zip code level, and this impact is highly dependent on the study area. In one study area (Kane County), block-level coefficients were very similar to those estimated on the basis of zip code data; whereas in the other study area (Peoria County), the two sets of coefficients differed substantially raising the possibility of drawing inaccurate inferences about the association between distance to mammography and late-stage cancer risk.

Conclusions
Spatial aggregation error can significantly affect the coefficient values and inferences drawn from statistical models of the association between cancer outcomes and spatial and non-spatial variables. Relying on data at the zip code level may lead to inaccurate findings on health risk factors.

publications.title: Healthcare Access, Socioeconomic Factors and Late-Stage Cancer Diagnosis: An Exploratory Spatial Analysis and Public Policy Implication
publications.publishedAt: International Journal of Public Policy · Jan 1, 2010
publications.description: Patients diagnosed with late-stage cancer have lower survival rates than those with early-stage cancer. This paper examines possible associations between several risk factors and late-stage diagnosis for four types of cancer in Illinois: breast cancer, prostate cancer, colorectal cancer, and lung cancer. Potential risk factors are composed of spatial factors and nonspatial factors. The spatial factors include accessibility to primary healthcare and distance or travel time to the nearest cancer screening facility. A set of demographic and socioeconomic variables are consolidated into three nonspatial factors by factor analysis. The Bayesian model with convolution priors is utilised to analyse the relationship between the above risk factors and each type of late-stage cancer while controlling for spatial autocorrelation. The results for breast cancer suggest that people living in neighbourhoods with socioeconomic disadvantages and cultural barriers are more likely to be diagnosed at a late stage. In regard to prostate cancer, people in regions with low socioeconomic status are also more likely to be diagnosed at a late stage. Diagnosis of late-stage colorectal or lung cancer is not significantly associated with any of the abovementioned risk factors. The results have important implications in public policy.

publications.title: Late-Stage Breast Cancer Diagnosis and Health Access in Illinois
publications.description: The variations of breast cancer mortality rates from place to place reflect both underlying differences in breast cancer prevalence and differences in diagnosis and treatment that affect the risk of death. This article examines the role of access to health care in explaining the variation of late-stage diagnosis of breast cancer. We use cancer registry data for the state of Illinois by zip code to investigate spatial variation in late diagnosis. Geographic information systems and spatial analysis methods are used to create detailed measures of spatial access to health care such as convenience of visiting primary care physicians and travel time from the nearest mammography facility. The effects of spatial access, in combination with the influences of socioeconomic factors, on late-stage breast cancer diagnosis are assessed using statistical methods. The results suggest that for breast cancer, poor geographical access to primary health care significantly increases the risk of late diagnosis for persons living outside the city of Chicago. Disadvantaged population groups including those with low income and racial and ethnic minorities tend to experience high rates of late diagnosis. In Illinois, poor spatial access to primary health care is more strongly associated with late diagnosis than is spatial access to mammography. This suggests the importance of primary care physicians as gatekeepers in early breast cancer detection.

Factors Affecting Transfer of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons from Made Tea to Tea Infusion
publications.publishedAt: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry · Jan 1, 2006
publications.description: Factors affecting transfer percentages of 12 polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) were investigated, including tea variety, tea/water ratio (TWR, g/mL), brewing times, washed tea or unwashed tea, and covered cup or uncovered cup. It was observed that %PAH transfer varied with tea variety and increased with the decrease of TWR. The mean %PAH transfer with TWR = 1/150 was 1.12 and 1.65 times higher than that with TWR = 1/100 and 1/50, respectively. %PAH transfer reduced greatly as the brewing times increased. The mean %PAH transfer in the first brewing time occupied 51.6% of the total three mean %PAH transfers in the three brewing times. The mean %PAH transfer decreased by 30.4% after the tea had been washed immediately before brewing. Brewing the tea within uncovered cup diminished %PAH transfer by a degree of 4.31−31.7% compared to brewing the tea within a covered cup.

publications.title: A network simulation of OTC markets with multiple agents
publications.description: We present a novel agent-based approach to simulating an over-the-counter (OTC) financial market in which trades are intermediated solely by market makers and agent visibility is constrained to a network topology. Dynamics, such as changes in price, result from agent-level interactions that ubiquitously occur via market maker agents acting as liquidity providers. Two additional agents are considered: \textit{trend investors} use a deep convolutional neural network paired with a deep Q-learning framework to inform trading decisions by analysing price history; and \textit{value investors} use a static price-target to determine their trade directions and sizes. We demonstrate that our novel inclusion of a network topology with market makers facilitates explorations into various market structures. First, we present the model and an overview of its mechanics. Second, we validate our findings via comparison to the real-world: we demonstrate a fat-tailed distribution of price changes, auto-correlated volatility, a skew negatively correlated to market maker positioning, predictable price-history patterns and more. Finally, we demonstrate that our network-based model can lend insights into the effect of market-structure on price-action. For example, we show that markets with sparsely connected intermediaries can have a critical point of fragmentation, beyond which the market forms distinct clusters and arbitrage becomes rapidly possible between the prices of different market makers. A discussion is provided on future work that would be beneficial.

publications.title: Computer-aided diagnostic screen for Congenital Central Hypoventilation Syndrome with facial phenotype
publications.description: Congenital Central Hypoventilation Syndrome (CCHS) has devastating consequences if not diagnosed promptly. Despite identification of the disease-defining gene PHOX2B and a facial phenotype, CCHS remains underdiagnosed. This study aimed to incorporate automated techniques on facial photos to screen for CCHS in a diverse pediatric cohort to improve early case identification and assess a facial phenotype–PHOX2B genotype relationship.

publications.title: Dynamical Analysis of Spatial Interaction Models
publications.description: We develop a novel dynamical method to examine spatial interaction models (SIMs). For each SIM, we use our dynamical framework to model emigration patterns. We look at the resulting population distributions to see if they are realistic or not. We use the US census data from 2010 and various spatial statistics to access the success or failure of each model. While we looked at over eighty different SIMs, we will focus here on two examples: the production constrained gravity model and the Radiation model. The results suggest that all these models fail to produce realistic population distributions and we identify the flaws within existing models. This leads us to suggest that we should define site attractiveness in terms of a second short range SIM leading to a new spatial interaction model - the Two-Trip model - which offers significant improvements when examined via our method. We also note that our Two-Trip adaptation can be used in any spatial modelling contexts, not just emigration.

publications.title: An undergraduate experiment demonstrating the physics of metamaterials with acoustic waves and soda cans
publications.description: We describe a novel undergraduate research project that highlights the physics of metamaterials with acoustic waves and soda cans. We confirm the Helmholtz resonance nature of a single can by measuring its amplitude and phase response to a sound wave. Arranging multiple cans in arrays smaller than the wavelength, we then design an antenna that redirects sound into a preferred direction. The antenna can be thought of as a new resonator, composed of artificially engineered meta-atoms, similar to a metamaterial. These experiments are illustrative, tactile, and open ended so as to enable students to explore the physics of matter/wave interaction.

projects.title: Sales Forecasting Analysis, The University of Chicago
projects.description:
GitHub: github.com/linpyl/Forecasting-Weight_Control_Product

 Conceptualized, built, and implemented models to forecast the sales of a weight-control dietary product based on the historic monthly sales and advertising expenditures data. By means of R program, I generated, tested, and validated several models (linear Regressions, Random Forest, ARIMA, Seasonal ARIMA, Support Vector Machine, and Ensemble Modeling Approaches) using time-series cross-validation approach. The forecasting models can be adopted as a base line to predict future demand upon which to make sales plans.

projects.title: Prediction of West Nile Virus Presence, The University of Chicago
projects.description:
GitHub: github.com/linpyl/Kaggle_West_Nile_Virues

 	KAGGLE COMPETITION. Applying statistical methods (Logistic and Poisson Regressions), regularization methods (lasso and best subset regressions), and machine learning algorithms (Neural Nets, Bagging, Random Forest, Boosting, and Support Vector Machine) along with two-stage strategy with given weather and location data to predict when and where different species of mosquitos will test positive for West Nile Virus. I designed the experiments and working flow, wrote the R codes that can run the predictions automatically in parallel on Midway computer cluster in the Super Computer Center of the University of Chicago, summarized and presented the research results. The prediction can serve as a basis for scheduling pesticide spraying at target locations beforehand in order to prevent the outbreaks of West Nile Virus.

projects.title: Survival Analysis, The University of Chicago
projects.description:
GitHub: github.com/linpyl/Prediction_of_Survivability_Rate

 Created a statistical (Logistic Regression) model as well as applied different data mining techniques (Decision Tree, Naïve Bayesian, Support Vector Machine) using R to predict survivability rate of breast cancer patients with 80% prediction accuracy. To perform the analysis, I queried the Cancer Incidence Public-Use Database to identify patients diagonized for the all the available years (1973-2010) with breast cancer in the United States. The models were adjusted for the selected explanatory variables. The final model can provide doctors as a standard way of discussing a person's prognosis. In addition, the accurate prediction in this project can serve as a base line for the purpose of effective use of limited health care resources.

projects.title: Strategy to Optimize TV Advertising Effectiveness, The University of Chicago
projects.description:
GitHub: github.com/linpyl/Yoplait_TV_Advertising_Analysis

 	Demonstrated strategies for Yoplait to enhance the effectiveness of its TV advertising based on moment-to-moment emotional data using SPSS Statistics. By applying Principle Component Analysis, Exploratory Factor Analysis, Multiple Discriminant Analysis, and Logistic Regression, the analysis successfully measured the total effectiveness of the TV advertising: who it’s reaching, how it’s resonating, and consumers’ reactions. These kinds of insights provided with the possibility to grow advertising in order to make a significant impact and maximize the return on investment.

 Analyzed and built customer segmentation based on the moment-to-moment emotional evaluations using SPSS. By combining aggregated, anonymous demographic information from participating data providers, I had identified who were the main competitors in the market as well as the key target segments who were more likely to resonate with the TV advertisements using Principle Component Analysis, k-Nearest Neighbors algorithm, Correspondence Analysis, and Logistic Regressions. These segments can be used as a base line to more efficiently deploy resources and develop messaging that resonates with particularly segments.

publications.title: Returning to the Workforce
publications.publishedAt: The Eleusis of Chi Omega · Apr 1, 2005
publications.description:
Women return to the workforce for many reasons: because there's a change in family circumstances due to divorce or death of a spouse, for a new challenge when children are in school, or to pay college tuition. In returning to work, we are faced with the dilemma of selling a developed skill set for which many of us have never been financially compensated.

Homemakers and women who volunteer have incredible multi-tasking skills. They are doers, decision makers, and decision implementers who work when they don't feel well and are rarely validated for their very real contributions to family and community.

How do you translate that experience to the job market? How do you get started? How do you maintain the balance of life that is so important?

headline: Senior Financial Crime Compliance and Program Management
about:
International expertise in ensuring compliance/regulatory readiness for financial services organizations.

I am an experienced, dedicated, organized and results-oriented Compliance professional with an extensive background in successfully managing compliance based projects in the financial services sector for over 15 years. Very recently headed the KYC onboarding function at a large local UAE based bank. As a Senior Manager with with the BIG 4, led and managed large and complex assignments assisting clients in adherence to compliance regulations and expectations, AML/CFT policies and procedures, risk assessments, investigations, analytics and reporting, etc. At EY, I successfully led and delivered large scale Sanctions lookback investigations and represented banking clients during interactions with OFAC, DoJ and other US regulators as part of my responsibilities. I also led and participated in client meetings and conferences related to financial crime compliance in the region.

Prior to assignments in the Middle East, I spent over 11 years in New York. While at Citibank I was trusted with a broad range of responsibilities within the KYC Utility, which including creating global KYC metrics to identify areas of key risks, business analyst for the CitiKYC One platform representing KYC Utility, in addition to responding to critical internal and external audit related matters among other tasks. Prior to that as a senior consultant with EY New York, I managed a number of complex projects in the compliance/regulatory technology projects implementing AML systems, analyzing monitoring scenarios, helping clients clear large alert backlogs, fine-tuning their scenarios to effectively manage alerts population, etc.

I am fortunate to have worked with Fortune 500 companies throughout my career and gaining international experience in compliance related roles with reputable financial institutions, which I’m now keen to build upon. My significant expertise is complemented by a MBA in Finance, in addition to excellent project management skills, multi-tasking, leadership abilities, stakeholder communication, and problem solving skills.

publications.title: Enhancing Power Network Robustness and Efficiency through Network Analysis and Probabilistic Simulation
publications.publishedAt: Interdisciplinary Conference on Electrics and Computer - INTCEC 2024 · Jul 30, 2024
publications.description: This study investigates the current state of the US power grid and identifies potential seasonal vulnerabilities using simulation and optimization. Extensive regional power flow analyses and seasonal investigations are conducted, modeling seasonal behavior as directed graphs utilizing historical data (2022) from the Energy Information Administration (EIA). Probabilistic simulations provide an environment to assess flow planning dynamics, highlighting deviations, and informing strategic planning efforts. Additionally, simulated attacks on each region are implemented, quantifying their impact on system cost through ‘knock-down’ computational experiments. This approach delivers valuable insights into regional network dynamics and pinpoints key areas for optimized planning throughout the year. By integrating network analysis, probabilistic simulation, and optimization, the findings of this study hold significant potential for enhancing grid resilience and optimizing resource utilization in power networks.

publications.title: Machine Learning Overbooking Framework for Outpatient Appointments: Improving Resource Allocation and Correcting Socioeconomic Bias
publications.description:
With the rise of artificial intelligence, the combination of strategies such as overbooking with ML models has emerged as a promising approach. However, there are concerns regarding group bias and its potential to result in unfair services, perpetuating historical barriers and disparities that society is striving to eliminate.

In the ML-enabled overbooking framework proposed in this study, we demonstrate the presence of socioeconomic group bias due to under-representation of a socioeconomically vulnerable population within the dataset, and how this worsens the service quality for the vulnerable group. We illustrate how including post-modeling strategies in the two proposed overbooking methodologies can completely mitigate this effect, ensuring fairness in the framework that combines overbooking and ML while improving resource efficiency.

projects.title: Forced Distribution Ranking System influence on organizational performance
projects.description:
Using simulations to study performance appraisal (PA) format, we extend the work of Scullen, 
Bergby, and Aiman-Smith (2005) by comparing the benefits of using different variations of a 
forced distribution ranking system (FDRS) with termination consequences to a PA system

probationary periods rather than a using traditional Rank and Yank system, a temporary Rank

publications.title: Sensitivity Analysis of Flexible Pavement Sections Using  Mechanistic-Empirical Pavement Design Guide
publications.publishedAt: International Journal of Pavement Research and Technology · Nov 1, 2015
publications.description:
The study evaluated the influence of four input parameters, namely, reliability level, climate, traffic characteristics and modulus values on the performance of selected pavement sections using MEPDG software. Knowledge gained from the sensitivity analysis of different pavement sections using MEPDG is expected to be useful to pavement designers and others using MEPDG for future pavement design. Specifically, this paper focuses on the sensitivity study of flexible pavement sections at four different locations namely, Chicago in Illinois, Grand Forks in North Dakota, Oklahoma City in Oklahoma, and Houston in Texas, for addressing sensitivity towards climatic conditions. For addressing effect of reliability and traffic three levels of reliability (80%, 90%, 95%) and traffic (low, medium, high) were used, respectively, for designing flexible pavement sections. Additionally, sensitivity towards modulus of sub grade soil was evaluated by designing pavement sections containing 6% lime, 15% class C fly ash (CFA), and 
15% cement kiln dust (CKD). The performance of each pavement section was monitored for 240 months (20 years) using MEPDG software by generating plots for rutting, alligator cracking, and International Roughness Index (IRI). It was found that rut predicted by MEPDG is sensitive towards climate, modulus values of chemically stabilized layer and reliability level. IRI values showed sensitiveness toward only reliability and traffic level. Alligator cracking showed sensitiveness toward climate with unexpected trend, modulus of chemically stabilized layer, reliability and traffic level.

publications.title: Jet-Fuel Production from Municipal Waste Streams: Process, Concerns, and Need for Standardization in Life Cycle Analyses
publications.publishedAt: Association of Technology, Management, and Applied Engineering · Aug 1, 2013
publications.description: Growth in worldwide air travel has prompted concern about the influence of aviation activities on the environment. In this work, we first provide an overview of the proposed technical process for converting waste to jet fuel. Potential benefits and concerns regarding the use of municipal waste streams as feedstock are then discussed. Note that reductions in greenhouse gas emissions using this alternative fuel source are dependent on the composition of the waste stream and the total system transportation requirements, which are site-specific and require further investigation via life cycle analysis models. We conclude by examining specific areas which could improve the usability of the results obtained from the life cycle analysis models.

**After working in Margins, I was offered Senior Analyst role in my previous position held 11/1/2013 - 7/31/2015**

- Responsible for opening and maintaining Futures and OTC Clearing Accounts.

- Liaison between Margins and Onboarding departments for initiatives to increase efficiency across both teams.

- Project Lead for deployment of new IRS product under the EUREX exchange.

- Organizing and leading weekly phone calls with large Investment Advisors.

- Extensive knowledge of documentation requirements for multiple entity types including hedge funds, mutual funds, investment advisors and foreign banks.

- Knowledge of Credit, Legal and Know Your Customer procedures for onboarding new entities.

- Frequent conversations with legal and compliance officers at large Investment Advisors in regard to documentation, procedures and account opening.

- Extensive experience reviewing documentation and pulling pertinent information in a timely manner.

- Experience with dealing with multiple Market Functions including Billing, Client Services, Client Executives and Salespersons.

- Chairman of Operation Excellence Risk and Control Committee which is tasked to review and improve complex processes across various work streams.

- Extensive work with Application Developers and Business Analysts to help guide the technical direction of main system Onboarding Master Central.

- Full knowledge of SAP Based System to pull back end reporting using complex SQL.

experience.position: Futures and Cleared OTC Margin Specialist
experience.description:
- Responsible for agreeing daily Initial Margin, Variation Margin and Collateral movements for Futures/OTC Accounts.

- Responsible for multiple “Platinum” and top tier client portfolios.

- Responsible for large client handled by multi-tiered exception process.

- Responsible for creation, review and approval of cash wires, collateral payments and internal journals.

- Responsible for review and potential restriction of accounts with aged margin calls.

- Frequent conversations about complex issues with clients involving large dollar amounts in 12+ currencies.

- High risk environment with large cash and collateral transactions.

- Advanced knowledge of Cleared Derivatives products.

- Advanced knowledge of Reconciliation using historical data.

- Knowledge of regulatory requirements around Margin.

- Assisted in Yearly Internal and CME Audit.

- Experience with working with other departments at bank on a high-level including Client Services, Middle Office, Client Executives and Salesperson

- Extensive Knowledge of margin reporting from the Chicago Mercantile Exchange(CME), The London Clearing House(LCH) and the Intercontinental Exchange(ICE).

- Extensive Customer Service experience via Four Hours a Day Servicing Phone Calls.

- Service Phone Calls from Internal Employees with Fraud Concerns.

- Responsible for Monitoring Bank Transactions for potentially fraudulent activity.

- Management Experience of FraudNet, A System Used to Fight Online Fraud in Multiple Industries.

- Identifying Fraudulent Phone Calls via Verifying Know Your Customer Information.

- Assisting Business and Personal Customers with Internet Banking, Transactions, Information Compromises and Fraud.

- Extensive experience of reviewing transaction data to see Anti Money Laundering patterns.

- Numerous Special Projects for Senior Management.

- Knowledge of Anti Money Laundering and Know Your Customer Policies.

- Building of Information Used for Verification of Business Customers.

- Specialized responsibilities including escrow and high-risk clients.

- Consistently topped metrics for completed requests.
